display: Procurement officer for a boutique safari lodge group in Nairobi. I buy everything from linen to coffee for six lodges across Kenya and Tanzania, and I'm also a keen birder.

signals.text: I'm looking for a locally made guest-room soap in Kenya that is a proper amenity bar, not a decorative tourist-shop one.
A sustainability audit flagged that all our guest-room soaps are imported, and I have to propose a local alternative by the end of October.
Guests at our lodges keep asking for Kenyan-made amenities, and we currently can't point them to one.
I've gone through my whole vendor list and found no local soap maker I'd trust at lodge scale. I need to look outside my usual network.
Any soap supplier I take on has to deliver consistently across six lodges and invoice properly. Supply reliability matters more to me than novelty.
Our amenity budget is tight: the cost per room night can't rise more than about 10%, and a local, sustainable soap has to fit inside that.
We pay roughly KES 45 per bar today, and any local option above that needs a solid justification.
I'd like to hear from small Kenyan makers who could scale to steady lodge-sized orders but haven't had a buyer like us before.
My draft response to the audit is due in a few days, and I'd welcome a quick sample or spec sheet I can show my management.
I'm running a house renovation in Karen at the same time as a heavy work deadline, and I'm short on time and headspace.
A family member is recovering from hip surgery and I'm helping with her rehab at home.
I've just logged my 400th bird species and my field notebook is nearly full. I'd like to meet other birders.

offers.text: Procurement for six lodges: linen, toiletries, coffee, cleaning supplies and kitchen goods, bought at group scale.
A database of about 80 vendors across Kenya and Tanzania. I can introduce a good supplier to the right category of lodge buyer.
Experience negotiating bulk contracts in both Kenyan shillings and USD.
Knowledge of how a hospitality group's sustainability audit scores suppliers. I can tell a small producer what evidence they would need to pass.
Feedback to a new local supplier on packaging, consistency, invoicing and lead times from a hospitality buyer's point of view.
A real, repeating order channel into six safari lodges for suppliers who fit the quality, price and reliability bar.
Birdwatching knowledge of the Nairobi area, including Ngong forest. I can take a visitor out on a Sunday morning.

catchers.hypo: We're a small soap workshop outside Nairobi making cold-process bars from Kenyan shea, coconut and plant oils. We've only sold at markets and want to supply hotels but don't know how to start.
catchers.can: I can tell them what a lodge group needs in specs, volume, consistency and invoicing, and I can put a trial batch in front of the lodge managers.
catchers.confirm: Can your workshop reliably produce several thousand uniform bars a month and issue proper tax invoices?

catchers.hypo: I run a cooperative of women who make natural soap from locally sourced ingredients. We have a sustainability story but no hotel customers yet.
catchers.can: I can match them against the audit's local and sustainable criteria and say whether it's worth taking a sample to my GM.
catchers.confirm: Can you document where your ingredients come from, and do you hold or plan to hold a Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) mark?

catchers.hypo: I help small manufacturers get ready to sell to hotels and lodges, covering certification, packaging and costing. Would a buyer like you test one of my clients?
catchers.can: I can give candid buyer feedback on one candidate soap maker and describe what a pass or fail looks like on cost and consistency.
catchers.confirm: Is your client making a bathroom-grade bar at a unit price close to KES 45?

catchers.hypo: I manage purchasing at another lodge or hotel group in East Africa and I'm also being pushed to localise amenities. Can we compare notes on suppliers and pooled orders?
catchers.can: I can share what I've learned about the audit and the local market, and explore pooling a bulk order across groups.
catchers.confirm: Do you buy for a multi-property group, and would you consider pooling demand with another buyer?

catchers.hypo: I'm a physiotherapist or home-care nurse who works with older patients recovering from hip surgery at home in Nairobi. Do you know anyone who needs this?
catchers.can: I can pass this to my family, who are in exactly this situation, and I'd gladly read a recommendation.
catchers.confirm: Do you make home visits in the Nairobi area for hip-surgery recovery?

catchers.hypo: I'm a landscaper or garden designer who builds low-maintenance, accessible gardens for older people with limited mobility, including raised beds and paths.
catchers.can: I can introduce them to my family, whose house in Karen will need a garden that suits someone recovering from surgery.
catchers.confirm: Have you designed gardens in the Nairobi area that are safe for walkers or wheelchairs?

catchers.hypo: We supply roofing tiles and building materials in Nairobi with reliable delivery dates. Do you know anyone who has been let down by a supplier?
catchers.can: I'm renovating a house in Karen with late roof tiles, so I can look at an alternative supplier and pass a recommendation to my contractor.
catchers.confirm: Can you deliver roofing tiles in Nairobi within a week and hold the delivery date in writing?

catchers.hypo: I'm visiting Nairobi and want to see some good birds near the city, with a local who knows where to go. Would you share a morning?
catchers.can: I can take them to Ngong forest for a Sunday morning outing and share my species list.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to be at the forest by 6:00 am on a Sunday?

catchers.hypo: I'm a procurement professional at a Kenyan company and feel stuck between sustainability demands and cost-cutting. How did you cope?
catchers.can: I can talk it through from experience, and have a candid peer conversation about how I'm working through the same tension.
catchers.confirm: Are you in a purchasing role and facing a sustainability and cost conflict right now?

forbids.text: I won't switch to a supplier who can't guarantee consistent supply to all six lodges.
I won't work with suppliers who can't issue proper invoices.
I can't commit to a purchase before the group's audit and cost review has approved it.
I won't make promises to a supplier on behalf of my GM or finance team.
I don't take new vendors on trust. Samples and references come first.

projects.name: Local guest-amenity soap for the lodge group
projects.text: Replace imported guest-room soap across six lodges with a Kenyan-made, sustainable bar that meets the group's audit criteria.
roles_needed: Hospitality buyer willing to pool volumes

policy.t1: Audit findings, that guests are asking for local amenities, what a lodge buyer needs in quality, consistency and invoicing, and an introduction to the relevant category of lodge buyer.
policy.t2: The cost ceiling of 10% per room night and the current price per bar, once a supplier looks credible and I know who they are.
policy.never: My salary, my house finances, my employer's internal discussions, and any doubts about my career.
